proofs.text: Run `--all --quick` over a marked pytest test asserting `1 == 2`; verify the output holds `--- pytest output (last 60 lines) ---`, that pytest's own `1 failed` line is under it, and that the heading comes before `Evidence is missing`. Run `--all --quick` over a passing test; verify no such heading is printed

Run `--all --record --ci` with no runner temporary directory in the environment, over a project whose pytest test fails; verify `.purlin/runtime/report/logs/pytest.log` exists and holds the arm's own output including the command line the arm ran

rule_text: An arm that exits non-zero or is killed has the last 60 lines of its own output printed to stdout under `--- <arm> output (last 60 lines) ---` before the missing-evidence lines, and under `--ci` every arm's whole output is published as `logs/<arm>.log` in the dashboard directory

def test_a_failing_arm_prints_its_tail_before_the_missing_evidence(
            self, tmp_path):
        root = _pytest_project(tmp_path, body=(
            'import pytest\n\n'
            '@pytest.mark.proof("feat", "PROOF-1", "RULE-1")\n'
            'def test_bad():\n'
            '    assert 1 == 2\n'))
        _spec(root, 'feat')
        code, output = _run(root, '--all', '--quick')
        assert code == 1, output
        heading = '--- pytest output (last 60 lines) ---'
        assert heading in output, output
        assert '1 failed' in output, output
        assert output.index(heading) < output.index('Evidence is missing'), \
            output
tests.name: test_a_failing_arm_prints_its_tail_before_the_missing_evidence
reasons: expected value computed by same function as SUT

def test_an_arm_that_passed_prints_no_tail(self, tmp_path):
        root = _pytest_project(tmp_path)
        _spec(root, 'feat')
        code, output = _run(root, '--all', '--quick')
        assert code == 0, output
        assert 'output (last 60 lines)' not in output, output

def test_ci_publishes_each_arms_whole_output(
            self, tmp_path, record_run, monkeypatch, capsys):
        # Off a runner the dashboard goes into the project, which is where the
        # test reads it back. On a runner both variables are set, and the
        # published directory would be the runner's own.
        for variable in ('RUNNER_TEMP', 'AGENT_TEMPDIRECTORY'):
            monkeypatch.delenv(variable, raising=False)
        root = _pytest_project(tmp_path, body=(
            'import pytest\n\n'
            '@pytest.mark.proof("feat", "PROOF-1", "RULE-1")\n'
            'def test_bad():\n'
            '    assert 1 == 2\n'))
        _spec(root, 'feat')
        record_run(root, '--all', '--ci')
        capsys.readouterr()
        published = root / '.purlin' / 'runtime' / 'report' / 'logs'
        text = (published / 'pytest.log').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
        assert '-m pytest' in text, text
        assert '1 failed' in text, text
tests.name: test_ci_publishes_each_arms_whole_output
